AppFunctionAppMetadata.appfn:description:
Tasks.org manages the user's tasks, lists, tags, saved places and reminders on this device.
Things about this data model that are easy to get wrong: - Ids are local to this install. Never store them; resolve names to ids each session. - Rows reference each other by id, never by name. Resolve a name the user said to an id before acting on it, and do not read an id back to them. - A task belongs to exactly one list and sits at no more than one place, but carries any number of tags. - Reminders are one collection covering both kinds: a time reminder carries a trigger time or an offset, a location reminder carries a place and no timing. Arrival and departure are separate, independent reminders. - Every read is paged: it takes a limit and an offset, reports a total that ignores both, and flags whether more remain. There is no way to ask for all of them, so do not assume one call saw everything - a user can have hundreds of tags. - To count, ask for a limit of zero: the total comes back with no rows. Never list rows in order to count them. - Text search is a regular expression over a task's own title and notes. Narrow it to one of the two when you mean one, and escape a literal dot or slash. - Some lists are read-only. A task on one says so, and writing to it fails rather than quietly doing nothing. - Creating, updating and completing tasks are batch operations: each takes a list of tasks and runs as one transaction. Send the whole set rather than calling once per task. - A new task gets nothing you do not send - no priority, dates, recurrence, reminders or tags - and lands in the user's default list unless you name one. - Deleting a task deletes its subtasks with it, and no delete can be undone.
